title: My Calendar III
description: Brute force to optimized: re-collecting and re-sorting every mark on every call versus a persistent sorted map, inserting only the two new marks per booking.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Design a class representing a calendar that supports a book(start, end) operation, adding a new event covering [start, end). Return the maximum number of events that are ever concurrently overlapping at any single point in time, after this booking is added (a "k-booking" being k events all overlapping at once).

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["Every booking is a RANGE [start, end)","A sweep line: +1 at every start, -1 at every end, running total gives overlap count"],["The maximum overlap must be reported after EVERY new booking","A structure that supports fast incremental insertion, not a full re-sort each time"]]}

blocks.text: Every call to book(start, end) adds a new event. After each addition, report the largest number of events that overlap at any single instant, considering every booking made so far.

blocks.title: Analogy: Tracking the Busiest Moment in a Room Booking System
blocks.text: Picture a meeting room booking system where overlapping bookings are allowed (unlike a normal calendar), and after every new booking, the system needs to report the busiest moment ever, how many meetings were happening at once, at their peak overlap.

blocks.caption: A sweep line: +1 at every start, -1 at every end, running total gives the overlap

blocks.text: After each booking in order, the maximum overlap reported is [1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3]. The third booking, [10,40], overlaps both [10,20] and [50,60] is unrelated, but [10,40] and [10,20] together give an overlap of 2; by the fourth booking, [5,15] overlapping both [5,10] (added later) and [10,40], the overlap reaches 3.

Before re-checking every pair of bookings after each addition, notice that overlap counting is a classic sweep-line problem: only the START and END points of each event actually change the "currently active" count.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: Marking +1 at every event's start and -1 at every event's end, then sweeping left to right while keeping a running total, gives the number of currently active events at any point.

Observation 2: The maximum value that running total ever reaches, across the whole sweep, is exactly the maximum concurrent overlap.

Observation 3: After each new booking, the ANSWER may need to be recomputed, but the events from all previous bookings do not need to change position, only the two new marks need to be added to the existing sorted structure.

Observation 4: Using a structure that stays sorted as new marks are inserted, rather than re-sorting everything each time, avoids repeating the sorting work for every previous booking on every single new call.
This leads to maintaining a sorted map of time to delta, inserting just two new marks per booking, then sweeping the whole (already sorted) map to find the current maximum overlap.

Keep a list of every booking made so far. On each new booking, add it to the list, then collect start/end marks from EVERY booking (old and new), sort them from scratch, and sweep to find the maximum overlap.

items: Append the new booking to a list of all bookings made so far.
Collect a +1 mark at every booking's start and a -1 mark at every booking's end, across the ENTIRE list.
Sort all of these marks by time.
Sweep through them, maintaining a running total, and track the maximum value reached.

blocks.caption: Brute force flow: re-collect and re-sort every mark, old and new, on every single call

codes.python:
class MyCalendarThree:
    def __init__(self):
        self.bookings = []

    def book(self, start, end):
        self.bookings.append((start, end))
        events = []
        for s, e in self.bookings:                # re-collect marks from EVERY booking
            events.append((s, 1))
            events.append((e, -1))
        events.sort()                                # re-sort from scratch every call

        cur = best = 0
        for _, delta in events:
            cur += delta
            best = max(best, cur)
        return best

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Every booking ever made is stored, and its two marks are re-derived and re-sorted alongside every other booking's marks, on every single call.
This guarantees correctness, since the sweep always reflects the true, complete set of bookings, but repeats the same sorting work again and again.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n squared log n) across n calls, since each call re-sorts O(n) marks.
Space: O(n) for the stored bookings.

Limitation: the marks from all previous bookings are already correctly ordered relative to each other from the last call, only the two new marks actually need to find their place; re-sorting everything from scratch repeats work that a persistently sorted structure would avoid.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why re-sorting every call is wasteful: the relative order of all previously inserted marks never changes, only the two new marks from the current booking need to be placed correctly.

What structure keeps marks sorted incrementally: an ordered map (or a sorted structure supporting O(log n) insertion), where each key is a time point and its value is the net delta (start marks add, end marks subtract) at that point.

How to answer each call: insert (or increment) the delta at the new start and end times, then sweep the whole ordered structure once, tracking the running total and its maximum.

The core idea: maintain one persistent sorted map of time to delta across all calls, inserting only 2 new entries per booking, and sweep the whole structure once per call to find the current maximum overlap.

Maintain a sorted map from time to net delta. On each book(start, end) call, add 1 to the entry at start and subtract 1 from the entry at end (creating new entries if needed, which a sorted map places correctly automatically). Then sweep the entire map in sorted order, maintaining a running total, and return its maximum value.

blocks.caption: Optimized flow: insert just 2 new marks into a persistent sorted structure, then sweep once

codes.python:
from sortedcontainers import SortedDict

class MyCalendarThree:
    def __init__(self):
        self.deltas = SortedDict()          # persists across calls; only 2 new keys per booking

    def book(self, start, end):
        self.deltas[start] = self.deltas.get(start, 0) + 1
        self.deltas[end] = self.deltas.get(end, 0) - 1

        cur = best = 0
        for delta in self.deltas.values():    # sweep the whole (already sorted) structure once
            cur += delta
            best = max(best, cur)
        return best

blocks.text: Because the sorted map persists across calls, every previously inserted mark is already exactly where it needs to be; each new booking only ever inserts 2 new entries, each an O(log n) operation, instead of re-deriving and re-sorting every mark from every previous booking. Sweeping the map afterward still visits every mark once, but none of that work is spent re-sorting.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(log n) per insertion, plus O(n) to sweep the map, so O(n) per call, O(n squared) across n calls total, a real improvement since the O(log n) sorting cost per mark is no longer repeated for every older mark on every call.
Space: O(n) for the sorted map.

blocks.text: My Calendar III is a sweep-line overlap-counting problem where the key optimization is persistence: keeping the marks from every previous call already sorted, and only ever inserting the two new marks for the current call, instead of rebuilding the whole sorted structure from scratch each time.

items: Rebuilding the list of events from scratch on every call instead of maintaining a persistent sorted structure across calls.
Forgetting that start and end marks at the SAME time point must combine correctly (summed, not overwritten) when multiple bookings share a boundary.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "can you avoid re-sorting every call", think: keep one persistent sorted map across calls, inserting only the 2 new marks each time.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The brute force runs in O(n log n) time per call (re-sorting every time). The optimized persistent sorted map runs in O(n) time per call (O(log n) insertion plus an O(n) sweep), avoiding redundant re-sorting.

items: Pattern: sweep-line overlap counting with a persistent sorted structure across calls.
Core Idea: maintain one sorted map of time to delta across all bookings, inserting only the 2 new marks per call, then sweep it once to find the current maximum overlap.
Time: O(n log n) per call for the brute force, O(n) per call for the optimized approach.
Most Important Observation: previously inserted marks never need to be re-sorted; only the two new marks per booking need to find their place.
Interview Difficulty: the sweep-line idea is standard; recognizing the persistence optimization is the detail that separates a working solution from an efficient one.
One line memory trick: plus 1 at start, minus 1 at end, kept in a persistent sorted map, swept once per call.
